decisions.decision: Branched fresh main from v1.5 after broken working tree
decisions.rationale: Clock Drift refactor attempts on master corrupted the working prototype; fresh branch from a known-good tag was cleanest reset. master branch preserved with all post-v1.5 work as cherry-pickable history.

engines[0]=smooth (slewed audio), engines[1]=scratch (target computation for [0]), engines[2]=instant (audio with direct register writes). Engine Blend continuously crossfades [0]/[2] outputs. Different goal from the abandoned dual-engine crossfade — that was for transition smoothing, this is for creative blend.

decisions.decision: Granular Haze feeds reverb INPUT, not output mix
decisions.rationale: Pre-feeding the reverb with stretched echoes of its own tail creates a self-reinforcing texture (with safety clamp to prevent runaway). Cleaner than parallel mix because the grain content gets shaped by the reverb itself rather than being layered raw.

decisions.decision: Paulstretch-style time stretch (independent playhead, unity-rate grains)
decisions.rationale: Naive granular slowdown via fractional-rate playback creates tape-pitch-down artifact. Solution: keep grain playback rate at 1.0 (no pitch shift), advance a separate playhead through the buffer at the freeze-controlled rate. Preserves pitch while elongating time.

decisions.decision: Soft limiter chosen over hard runaway prevention
decisions.rationale: User wanted to preserve ability to generate sustained feedback as a creative effect. Side-channel limiter on output bounds L/R divergence (the 'blow out one ear' issue) while leaving mid content untouched, so feedback can still build up musically.

Lower asymptote (0.06) than knee threshold (0.125) means tanh kicks in at the 'feels right' point but compresses harder afterward — gives more redistribution toward center on hard-pan content without changing the limiter onset feel.

next_action: Decide whether to bring forward more functionality from master (crackle fix, morph speed knob, Error Accumulator prototype) or continue exploring the granular/blend axis. Listen-test current build with diverse source material to identify next refinement.
context_notes: This is a creative DSP exploration session, not a formal GSD phase. The architecture started as 'morph between commits' (smooth↔click) and grew into a multi-axis texture engine with feedback grain loop and stereo-balance-aware limiting. Sound character: the Engine Blend dimension lets you choose between glide and stutter morph behavior; Haze adds sustained granular feedback that shapes the reverb tail; Freeze stretches the grain timebase without pitch shift (paulstretch). Side-channel limiter protects ears during morph squeals.
